notes: Unknown or unreported engineering values are null. Do not convert average science data return into instrument storage capacity.
Published piece masses are summed only where NASA lists subassemblies separately; summed values are labeled derived.
Game balance values must be stored separately and marked as game assumptions.

components.name: Perseverance rover (complete vehicle)
components.purpose: Carry instruments, mobility, sampling system and compute/power subsystems across Mars surface.
components.mass_status: NASA-published total rover mass; not a bare chassis mass
limitations: Full rover system mass; do not use as chassis-only mass.

components.name: Perseverance chassis/frame
components.purpose: Structural chassis, equipment deck and belly pan.
limitations: NASA page describes structure but does not give a separate frame mass.

components.name: Mastcam-Z
components.purpose: Zoom stereo imaging, panoramas, color imagery and video.
limitations: Data return is an average operational return, not a fixed file-size limit.

components.name: SuperCam
components.purpose: Remote imaging, laser-induced spectroscopy and chemical/mineral analysis of rocks and soils.
components.mass_status: sum of 5.6 kg mast head + 4.8 kg body spectrometers + 0.2 kg calibration assembly
components.data_basis: per experiment; NASA also reports about 4.2 Mbit/day
limitations: Reported component masses are summed from NASA-listed subassemblies.

components.name: PIXL
components.purpose: Close-range X-ray elemental chemistry and microscopic texture imaging.
components.mass_status: sum of 4.3 kg sensor head + 2.6 kg body electronics + 0.015 kg calibration target
components.data_basis: per experiment; NASA also reports about 2 MB/day
limitations: Requires robotic-arm placement close to the rock.

components.name: SHERLOC + WATSON
components.purpose: UV Raman/fluorescence and organic/mineral mapping; WATSON close-up color context imaging.
components.mass_status: sum of turret assembly 3.11 kg + body 1.61 kg
limitations: Arm-mounted; combined power is sum of the turret and body published figures.

components.name: RIMFAX
components.purpose: Subsurface radar profiling along rover traverse.
limitations: Penetration exceeds 10 m depending on material; measurement interval about 10 cm along track.

components.name: MEDA
components.purpose: Measure wind, air temperature, humidity, pressure, radiation and atmospheric dust.
components.data_basis: NASA page does not specify interval for the 11 MB figure

components.name: Multi-Mission Radioisotope Thermoelectric Generator
components.purpose: Provide steady electrical power and thermal energy.
components.power_status: about 110 W electrical at launch, declining a few percent per year
limitations: Power value is beginning-of-mission output, not current output. Two rechargeable Li-ion batteries support peak loads.

components.name: Perseverance rechargeable battery pair
components.purpose: Buffer activity peaks that exceed the MMRTG steady output.
limitations: Battery-pair mass 26.5 kg and ~43 Ah each verified in press kit p.38. Usable Wh not specified; capacity_wh stays null.
components.confidence: published pair mass and count; approximate per-battery Ah; usable Wh unknown

components.name: Solar array (generic mission option)
components.purpose: Photovoltaic electrical generation for a mission design option.
limitations: Not used by Perseverance; configure from a separately sourced spacecraft design rather than treating as Mars 2020 hardware.

components.name: Rover thermal control/heaters
components.purpose: Keep rover systems in operating temperature ranges; MMRTG waste heat contributes thermal energy.
limitations: Separate heater mass/power is not provided on the cited NASA component page.

components.name: UHF rover-to-orbiter and orbiter-to-Earth relay
components.purpose: Send rover science and engineering data through Mars orbiters to Earth/DSN.
limitations: Perseverance antenna subsystem mass and power are not quantified in the cited sources; relay-network throughput is in relay_plans.json.

components.name: Terrain-Relative Navigation (TRN) / Lander Vision System
components.purpose: Match descent images to onboard terrain maps and select a reachable safe touchdown target.
limitations: The 600 m value is maximum change to touchdown target, not guaranteed landing error.

package_note: Snapshot reference with per-field units in names; null means unavailable, never zero. See docs/PHYSICS.md and source URLs.
